title: Steam likely did not ban AI art in games due to copyright
author: Ok-Company-5016
selftext:
I saw a post that explained this on the Steamworks forum.

>I do not believe this because there is no court of law that will rule anything as infringing copyright by "eyeballing" it because that was what the Steamworks reviewer did.  
>  
>I asked very clearly how they arrive at that conclusion because it's very clear when they said my text was AI, they were just eyeballing it, they refuse to prove it then retired my game.  
>  
>Currently right now, it's literally impossible to prove anything is AI generated conclusively in the court of law if the person simply choose to deny it, I know because there is a game released on 21st of June that is AI but they eyeballed it and thought it was human done.  
>  
>There are a lot more AI games right now on Steam that is still up, so if the issue was copyright and AI, then all these games would have already been taken down to avoid copyright.  
>  
>The issue is someone personally who has a problem with AI right now.  
>  
>Right now, there is someone at the review team doing this on their own volition because of how unprofessional the evaluation has been and the lack of updates to their policy, and the fact all these other games with AI gen assets got through previously being still up.  
>  
>I read a day back apparently a game called Chaos Head Noah got held up by a Steam reviewer for similar reason, and they made the original decision to reject the game rather than policy and when people protested, things finally went through.  
>  
>Now of course this is all speculation but there is a double standard here, and absolutely zero professionalism in evaluation which means this cannot be standard company procedure.  
>  
>I may be wrong and eat crow on this but the contradictory and nonsensical nature of this whole debacle cannot be something done with intelligent intentions.

I do agree this seems like a solo decision and there is no real way to prove this in the court of law.

Source: [https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/discussions/0/6717729816413966581/?ctp=2](https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/discussions/0/6717729816413966581/?ctp=2)

comments.author: featherless_fiend
comments.body: I can't view the link. Are you seriously telling me someone had their game rejected for AI text?

replies.author: Ok-Company-5016
replies.body: Apparently so but it might not even be AI text.

comments.author: potterharry97
comments.body:
I don't think it's just a sole reviewer, at least not anymore, Steam has released a statement about this now:

`In a statement emailed to The Verge, Valve PR representative Kaci Boyle said the company’s goal is “not to discourage the use of [AI] on Steam; instead, we’re working through how to integrate it into our already-existing review policies.” She went on to say that the company’s current review process takes into account current copyright law, and that “while developers can use these AI technologies in their work... they can not infringe on existing copyrights.”`

`Boyle added that Steam will refund app-submission credits for any developers whose games were rejected over AI copyright issues as the company refines its review process. It made the same offer to potterharry97.`

replies.author: Ok-Company-5016
replies.body: That makes no sense though, what is infringing on existing copyrights when no one can prove what copyright they infringed on? I want to know what they mean by refining the current review process.

replies.author: potterharry97
replies.body: Yeah I read some comments that right now they're sort of just determining what's AI or not by "eyeballing" it. So like I have no idea how sustainable that is and there's bound to be some false positives. The argument in terms of infringement is that the content generated by an AI that was trained in copyrighted material is also liable to be infringing on copyright. So the future handling of it will be based on whether legal systems consider that sort of content infringement or not.

replies.author: Ok-Company-5016
replies.body: It is still objectively impossible to prove which pictures lead to the generation of a particular image if the person does not declare it as AI-generated, and just generally impossible to determine overall.

replies.author: potterharry97
replies.body: Yeah, the whole thing is sort of a mess rn, but it is what it is

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: I wonder if there's some info we are missing. Currently it sounds like a catch-22 banning all AI assets, but why that game? Did it obviously break copyright, by being something like ghibli style or including spiderman as a placeholder?

replies.author: Ok-Company-5016
replies.body: They gave the reasoning as it just being AI assets "with copyrighted images in the training set" and nothing else. It's extremely stupid which is why it's being brought up again.

replies.author: Silent_Dragonfly_413
replies.body: I believe the game banned, according to his YouTube channel, was a low effort hentai puzzle game. The likely reason his game was rejected was that it had anime characters that too closely resembled anime characters from copyrighted IPs. I don't think the AI ban will effect someone who used a AI generated skybox or 3D texture for example. It possibly wouldn't even effect AI anime characters if they are original enough.

replies.author: suby
replies.body:
The first comment in this thread chain is the OP of the thread which kicked off this whole thing. 

https://www.reddit.com/user/potterharry97

He posted a video of one of his games and as you say, it is the lowest of low effort games, and a hentai game at that. I'm hoping this prompted them to be more skeptical than usual. Hell, in the description of the youtube video he writes, "In case you wanted to check out my blatant cash grabs:"

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m60pGapJ8ao

Presumably this is the rejected game
https://machpointgaming.itch.io/hentai-puzzles-attack-on-tight-panties

I don't think Valve should ban AI generated work on the grounds of copyright, but I also do not want Steam flooded with thousands of low effort AI generated trash each day, which is where this is eventually headed without some sort of gate keeping policy.

replies.author: potterharry97
replies.body: Yeah that was the rejected game. I genuinely mostly did it for shits and giggles and out of curiosity to see if I could, but other devs have mentioned similar rejections now, and not just hentai ones. So while I don't mind personally my low effort game getting taken down, Id really hate for Steam to take a 100% anti ai stance

replies.author: suby
replies.body: They are not 100% anti-ai. I don't know first hand but I've read that there are image generation models which claim to train on non-copyrighted material. I'm guessing that these generate poor quality images right now, but such ai generated content would be allowed.

replies.author: SpectreSunWorks
replies.body: It's extremely unclear. I have been trying to get in touch with their support but there has been no response but the game I was trying to publish is being stated as "copyright infringing" for no other reason than it being AI.

replies.author: potterharry97
replies.body: It's not 100% but at least based on the current state of things, it's like a 95% AI ban, and the 5% is reserved for people/companies with enough resources to train their own models, which is very few indie game devs i imagine, mostly just AAA companies.

replies.author: SpectreSunWorks
replies.body: This isn't true. The game he's talking about, in this thread is my game, and I don't have any hentai in the game but they retired it for AI anyway. [https://spectresunworks.itch.io/the-cyber-masquerade](https://spectresunworks.itch.io/the-cyber-masquerade)

comments.author: zxrzy97
comments.body: One of our games used AI material and voice, but it didn't affect Valve's review.

replies.author: Ok-Company-5016
replies.body: Not sure if it's changed now. But they might have thought it wasn't AI.
